from jobs import unique_jobs

def test_basic():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 't1'},
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 't2'},  # duplicate by (source,source_id)
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': '2', 'title': 't3'},
    ]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # should keep first of duplicate
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert res[0]['title'] == 't1'
    assert res[1]['title'] == 't3'
    # check order stable
    # rows list order preserved

def test_missing_source_id():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': None, 'title': 'm1'},
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': None, 'title': 'm2'},  # missing source_id
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 'n1'},
    ]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # both missing rows kept
    assert len(res) == 3
    # check order
    assert res[0]['title'] == 'm1'
    assert res[1]['title'] == 'm2'
    assert res[2]['title'] == 'n1'

def test_empty_source_id():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'B', 'source_id': '', 'title': 'e1'},
        {'source': 'B', 'source_id': '', 'title': 'e2'},
        {'source': 'B', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 'n1'},
    ]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(res) == 3  # both empty kept
    assert res[0]['title'] == 'e1'
    assert res[1]['title'] == 'e2'
    assert res[2]['title'] == 'n1'

def test_different_sources():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'X', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 'x1'},
        {'source': 'Y', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 'y1'},  # different source, same id
        {'source': 'X', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 'x2'},  # duplicate within X
    ]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # dedup by (source,source_id) only within same source
    # X:1 first row x1 kept, x2 ignored
    # Y:1 y1 kept
    # So result should be x1 and y1 (order stable)
    assert len(res) == 2
    # order should be x1 then y1 (since x1 first)
    assert res[0]['title'] == 'x1'
    assert res[1]['title'] == 'y1'

def test_no_mutation():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 't1'},
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': '1', 'title': 't2'},
    ]
    orig_rows = rows.copy()  # but rows might be dict list, shallow copy fine
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # ensure rows list not changed (no mutation of dicts)
    # simple check: rows[0]['title'] still 't1'
    assert rows[0]['title'] == 't1'
    assert rows[1]['title'] == 't2'

def test_complex():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'S1', 'source_id': None, 'title': 'M1'},
        {'source': 'S1', 'source_id': 'A', 'title': 'N1'},
        {'source': 'S1', 'source_id': 'A', 'title': 'N2'},  # duplicate N
        {'source': 'S2', 'source_id': None, 'title': 'M2'},
        {'source': 'S2', 'source_id': None, 'title': 'M3'},  # duplicate missing
        {'source': 'S2', 'source_id': 'B', 'title': 'N3'},
    ]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # missing rows all kept: M1, M2, M3
    # N1 kept (first A), N2 ignored
    # B kept
    # expected order: M1, N1, M2, M3, N3 (since M2,M3 appear after N1)
    # Actually order: row0 M1, row1 N1, row2 N2 ignored, row3 M2, row4 M3, row5 N3
    # So result should have 5 rows: M1, N1, M2, M3, N3
    assert len(res) == 5
    titles = [r['title'] for r in res]
    assert titles[0] == 'M1'
    assert titles[1] == 'N1'
    assert titles[2] == 'M2'
    assert titles[3] == 'M3'
    assert titles[4] == 'N3'

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_basic()
    test_missing_source_id()
    test_empty_source_id()
    test_different_sources()
    test_no_mutation()
    test_complex()
    print('All tests passed')
